subtopics.title: What a Control Account Is and Why We Need One

questions.question: The Debtors Control account exists to answer which question?
options: How much do all debtors owe the business in total?
Which single debtor owes the most?
How much cash is in the bank?
Which goods were returned this month?

questions.question: The standing principle of control accounts is:
options: Totals in the personal accounts, detail in control
Detail in the Debtors Ledger, totals in the control account — two views of the same facts
Only cash transactions are posted to control
Control accounts are only used at year end

questions.question: Debtors Control increases on the debit side because:
options: All control accounts are debit accounts
The journals only produce debit totals
Debtors are an asset — the account grows when debtors owe us more
The credit side is reserved for creditors

subtopics.title: Posting the Debit Side — When Debtors Owe Us More

questions.question: The opening balance of R18 700 on 1 August sits on the debit side because:
options: It is what debtors still owed from July — an asset balance
All opening balances are debits
It represents money the business owes
The bookkeeper chose that side

questions.question: The Debtors Journal total of R52 600 is posted to Debtors Control as:
options: A credit, contra account Bank
Individual invoices, one at a time
A credit, contra account Sales
One debit entry — credit sales make debtors owe us more

questions.question: Posting individual invoices to the control account is wrong because:
options: Invoices are never recorded anywhere
The control account receives journal totals only; invoices belong to the personal accounts
Invoices belong in the Cash Receipts Journal
The control account has no room for detail

subtopics.title: Posting the Credit Side — When Debtors Owe Us Less

questions.question: The R36 400 received from debtors is posted as:
options: Credit Debtors Control, contra account Bank
Debit Debtors Control, contra account Bank
Credit Bank, contra account Sales
Debit Bad Debts

questions.question: Writing off the R1 200 bad debt means:
options: The money was finally received
The debtor's balance doubles
The business absorbs the loss and stops overstating the asset — credit control, debit Bad Debts
The debt moves to the creditors ledger

questions.question: The debit side totals R71 300 and the credit side R40 700. The balance carried down is:
options: R30 600 written on the credit side, brought down as a debit balance
R30 600 written on the debit side, brought down as a credit balance
R40 700 on either side
R71 300 brought down

questions.question: The closing debit balance of R30 600 tells the owner:
options: The business owes debtors R30 600
Debtors as a group owe the business R30 600 at month end
R30 600 was received during August
R30 600 of sales were made in August

subtopics.title: The Agreement Check and the Creditors Mirror Image

questions.question: The month-end agreement check requires that:
options: The control balance equals the bank statement total
The Debtors Ledger equals the Creditors Ledger
Debtors Control equals Sales for the month
The list of individual debtors' balances totals exactly the control account balance

questions.question: In the Creditors Control account, credit purchases are posted as:
options: A credit — we owe more, and liabilities grow on the credit side
A debit — purchases are assets
No entry until payment
A debit to Bank

questions.question: The single question that gives the correct side for any control account entry is:
options: Which journal is largest this month?
Did this event make the amount owed grow or shrink?
Is the amount bigger than R1 000?
Was the transaction in cash?

questions.question: The pages answer 'what does Mr Sithole owe?' and the control line answers:
options: What does the whole street owe, in one number?
Which supplier must be paid first?
What did the business bank this week?
Which page has the neatest writing?

questions.question: The two records make a genuine control because:
options: They are written by the same person on the same day
The control line is copied from the pages weekly
They are built along different roads — daily lines versus monthly totals — yet must agree
Only one of them is ever used

questions.question: 'Counting the street twice' is described as:
options: Wasteful double work
A legal requirement only
A trick for faster posting
The street auditing itself — two independent counts that catch each other's errors

questions.question: R52 600 of credit sales go IN on the debit side because:
options: The street owes us more — more means debit
Sales are always debited
The money was received in cash
The credit side was full

questions.question: The R1 200 bad debt is a 'sad exit' on the credit side because:
options: The customer paid at last
The street owes us less even though not a cent arrived
It increases what debtors owe
Bad debts belong to creditors control

questions.question: August settles at R30 600 on the debit side, which means:
options: The business must pay out R30 600
August's sales totalled R30 600
The street owes the store R30 600 as September begins
The account made a profit of R30 600

questions.question: The pages total R31 800 but the control line says R30 600. The first correct response is:
options: Change the control balance to R31 800
Read the R1 200 gap as a clue and hunt the entry that travelled only one road
Write off the difference as a bad debt
Ignore it until year end

questions.question: In the story, the R1 200 disagreement arose because:
options: A payment was posted twice to control
The Debtors Journal was miscast
A customer paid in cash without a receipt
The bad-debt write-off reached the control totals but was never entered on the customer's page

questions.question: On the creditors side, the control machinery is identical except that:
options: The balance grows on the credit side and the question becomes: do we owe more, or less?
There are no personal accounts
The agreement check is yearly instead of monthly
Only cash purchases are recorded
